meta.title: CIP Forsta ETL — Connect, Extract, Transform, Load, Derive

cards.title: 1 · Connect
items: launchd runs scripts/weekly_forsta.py daily at 09:00 IST, plus Tue/Wed 14:00 and 23:30 IST: waves launch Monday 12–13 UTC and close Mon 20:00 – Wed 23:00 IST (median 13 h)
HTTPS to se1.decipherinc.com/api/v1 with the x-apikey header from .env; the key is never printed
GET only: rh/users/self (auth check), rh/companies/all/surveys, surveys/{path}/datamap, surveys/{path}/data. Retries connection errors, timeouts, 429 and 5xx

cards.title: 2 · Extract
items: Discover lists every survey and sets its state: due (closed, readable, not loaded), loaded, failed, hibernated (428), testing; a reopened survey becomes due again
Each due wave: datamap?format=json and data?format=json with no cond filter — every status, so dropout and terminates are kept; analysis uses qualified only
One survey = one wave: selfserve/58f/YYMMNN, labelled by the Monday of its first qualified completion

cards.title: 3 · Transform
items: Datamap read per question: single, multi, grid, bipolar (left/right statements), numeric, text; answer labels from the question or its variables; 'other (specify)' text becomes its own question; flags t (technical) and v (virtual, incl. '- NORMALIZED' copies)
Records: codes stay codes, numbers become finite decimals, text is kept as text, long strings are cut to the column size
userAgent, url, session, dcua and ipAddress are never stored; RID is kept only as sha256 respondent_key

cards.title: 4 · Load
items: The wave is 'loading' (invisible) while it loads. Definitions are upserted; respondents are upserted in one batch; answers are replaced in 5,000-row batches in one transaction; respondents Forsta removed are deleted
Verify: every record is a respondent, every datamap variable is a field, every field holds exactly as many answers as the payload. Pass → verified; fail → failed, retried next run
A failed reload never hides a verified wave whose data did not change

cards.title: 5 · Derive — nothing left for the UI
items: Profiles: age band 18-29 / 30-44 / 45-60 / over 60; generation GenZ 18-28, Millennial 29-44, GenX 45-60, Boomer 61+; age and income midpoints for averages
Harmonise: questions linked to concepts across waves and platforms; cohorts derived; cube cells for every answer × standard cut × cohort
cip_tracker_line rebuilds the data team's 'Weekly Line-By-Line' rows; checked against their file: 16 waves, identical except 3 defects in the file
cip_search indexed per wave; publications re-checked for drift
